body: Four fungi in a vegan capsule: Hericium erinaceus (lion's mane), Cordyceps militaris, Inonotus obliquus (chaga) and Ganoderma lucidum (reishi). The listing prints 100 per cent pure against each of them and names the shell as hydroxypropyl methylcellulose.
Three of the four are sold on their own here as well: lion's mane, chaga and reishi.
Two capsules a day, preferably with a meal, and at least 500 ml of water.
Two is the serving. If you miss a day, take two the next day rather than four.

ingredients.intro: The listing names four fungi and the shell, and prints 100 per cent pure against each of the four. What it does not print is how the 800 mg is divided between them.

cards.p: The white spined mass that grows out of old hardwood, usually beech or oak. It has no cap and no gills. We sell it on its own as well, and that label names the fruiting body. This one does not say which part is in the blend.

cards.alt: A small cluster of orange, finger shaped Cordyceps militaris fruiting bodies pushing up through leaf litter
cards.p: A small orange club fungus that fruits from buried insect pupae, and the one of the four that is usually farmed on grain or rice rather than gathered off wood.

cards.alt: A black chaga conk on a birch trunk
cards.p: The hard black mass on a living birch, cracked like charcoal outside and rust orange inside. On its own it is 750 mg a capsule. Here it is one of four and its share of the 800 mg is not printed.

cards.alt: Ganoderma lucidum growing on dead hardwood
cards.p: The varnished, kidney shaped bracket of dead and dying hardwood, hard rather than fleshy. The single jar is 50 at 800 mg, and that label does not name a part either.

cards.alt: Plain capsules and a wooden scoop on a slate board, a generated scene
cards.p: This is the only jar on the shelf whose listing names the shell material. Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose is made from plant cellulose, and it is what vegan capsule usually means when a label bothers to say. The capsules in the picture are a generated scene rather than a photograph of ours.

Lion's mane (Hericium erinaceus) · cordyceps (Cordyceps militaris) · chaga (Inonotus obliquus) · reishi (Ganoderma lucidum) · vegan capsule (hydroxypropyl methylcellulose). The listing prints 100 per cent pure against each of the four.

£39.99. One size. 50 capsules at two a day is 25 days, which works out at £1.60 a day.

Anyone who reacts to mushrooms: there are four in here and any of them can be the one. If you take medication that thins the blood, or insulin or another medicine for blood sugar, ask your GP or pharmacist first, because reishi, chaga and cordyceps are all routinely flagged for one or the other. Not for children. If you are pregnant or nursing, or you take prescribed medication, ask before you start.
spec.smallprint: Contains mushroom, which is an allergen for some people. Do not exceed the stated dose. Speak to your GP or pharmacist before starting any supplement, particularly if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or take medication. Food supplements should not be used as a substitute for a varied and balanced diet and a healthy lifestyle. Keep out of reach of young children.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: Four species named in Latin, the count, the milligrams, the capsule material and the serving are all printed. The split between the four is not, and it sits on the sheet as a blank. What any of them does in a person is not something we are permitted to say, so it is not on this page.

reiss.label: Reiss's turn
reiss.h2: Four mushrooms, and the number I would want
paras: Eight hundred milligrams, four fungi. The obvious question is how much of each, and the honest answer is that our listing does not say. Two hundred each would be a tidy way to make it. So would six hundred of one and a token of the other three. I cannot show you which this is, so the row on the sheet is empty and it will stay empty until the label fills it.
Four fungi, dried and milled into a capsule. The whole declared list is above, with nothing hidden behind a blend name.

If you want one fungus and one short label to read, the single jars are cheaper and simpler, and the lion's mane one names the part used. If you would rather have all four in one morning, this is the jar, and it costs a pound sixty a day.
reiss.pull: Nothing hidden behind a blend name.
